'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***[[2025 Uvira offensive]]
****[[Rwanda]]n-backed [[March 23 Movement|M23 rebels]] advance on the city of [[Butembo]], [[North Kivu]], and capture [[Kamanyola]] in [[South Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] after defeating [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese forces]]. Local officials say M23 forces are now preparing to advance on [[Uvira]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-un-children-killed-bukavu-rebels-0b72da70e3e96b1c100812443fc3201a (AP)]
****[[Burundi]] initiates the withdrawal of its [[National Defence Force (Burundi)|military forces]] from the eastern DRC following M23 advances. Between 10,000 and 15,000 Congolese civilians cross into Burundi to avoid violence, with several drowning in the [[Ruzizi River]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/rebel-held-ports-eastern-dr-congo-re-open-aid-needs-grow-2025-02-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[Gaza war]], [[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[January 2025 Gaza war ceasefire|2025 Gaza war ceasefire]]
***[[Hamas]] accuses [[Israel]] of carrying out at least 266 attacks in the [[Gaza Strip]] since the agreed [[ceasefire]] on January 19, killing at least 132 [[Palestinians]] and wounding 900 others. [https://www.newsweek.com/hamas-accuses-israel-nearly-270-ceasefire-violations-report-2029583 (Newsweek)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Al-Kadaris and Al-Khelwat massacres]]
***[[Rapid Support Forces]] militants kill at least 433 people in the villages of Al-Kadaris and Al-Khelwat, [[White Nile State]], [[Sudan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/sudans-rsf-kill-more-than-200-white-nile-lawyers-say-2025-02-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli invasion of Lebanon (2024–present)|Israeli invasion of Lebanon]]
**[[Israel]] partially withdraws [[Israel Defense Forces|troops]] from [[Lebanon]] as the deadline for their withdrawal expires. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/2/18/deadline-for-israeli-withdrawal-from-lebanon-expires (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Tomb of Thutmose II]]
**A joint [[Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities (Egypt)|Egyptian]]-[[United Kingdom|British]] archaeological mission announces the discovery of the tomb of King [[Thutmose II]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/egypt-discovery-king-thutmose-ii-ancient-royal-tomb/ (CBS News)]
*[[Cinema of China|Chinese]] [[animation|animated film]] ''[[Ne Zha 2]]'' amasses a total [[box office]] of [[renminbi|¥]]12.3 billion ([[US dollar|US$]]1.69 billion), surpassing ''[[Inside Out 2]]'' as the highest-grossing animated film globally. [https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/chinese-film-nezha-2-becomes-highest-grossing-animated-film-globally-2025-02-18/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[German economic crisis (2022–present)|German economic crisis]]
**[[Germany|German]] [[automotive industry|automotive]] parts company [[Continental AG]] announces it will [[layoff|lay off]] over 3,000 [[research and development]] positions and end operations at its [[factory]] in [[Nuremberg]], [[Bavaria]], by 2026. [https://www.dw.com/en/german-auto-parts-giant-to-slash-thousands-of-jobs/a-71664680 (DW)]
*[[Brazil]]ian [[Ministry of Mines and Energy (Brazil)|minister of mines and energy]] [[Alexandre Silveira]] announces that the country will join [[OPEC+]]. [https://apnews.com/article/brazil-oil-opec-cop30lula-3437780649f1d02bb041bd786131062e (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[February 2025 North American storm complex]]
**The death toll from flooding in [[Kentucky]], United States, rises to 14, amid the threat of an imminent [[winter storm]] in the region. [https://www.nbcnews.com/weather/winter-weather/death-toll-kentucky-storms-rises-14-state-braces-another-winter-weathe-rcna192586 (NBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[Russia–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] and [[Russia]] start talks in [[Saudi Arabia]] about the [[Russo-Ukrainian War|war in Ukraine]] without [[European Union|European]] or [[Government of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] participation. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/18/world/europe/us-russia-saudi-ukraine.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c743jl8k4kko (BBC News)]
**The delegations agree to start the negotiating process for ending the war, create high-level teams, and normalize [[Diplomatic relations|diplomatic]] and economic ties between the two countries. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-riyadh-talks-trump-putin-rubio-0c3beebfef5839e9d509ff58239a6bc5 (AP)]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] calls for a [[Next Ukrainian presidential election|new presidential election]] to be held in Ukraine as part of a peace deal with Russia. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/us/news/2025/02/18/zelensky-will-be-forced-hold-elections-under-us-russia-plan/ (''The Telegraph'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-says-ukraine-should-never-have-started-it-remarks-war-russia-rcna192710 (NBC News)]
**Russia rules out any [[peacekeeping|peacekeepers]] from [[NATO]] [[Member states of NATO|member states]] being stationed in Ukraine as part of any peace agreement. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cd0n5e1pdz9o (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Istanbul alcohol poisonings]]
**Over 124 people have been killed over the last six weeks from consuming [[Moonshine|bootleg alcohol]], with dozens still hospitalized. Twenty-eight people are arrested in connection with the production and distribution of the alcohol. [https://www.haarlemsdagblad.nl/buitenland/ruim-120-doden-door-illegale-alcohol-in-turkije/41616846.html (''Haarlems Dagblad'')] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bootleg-alcohol-kills-124-turkey-6-weeks/ (CBS News)]
*[[Animal welfare in the United Kingdom]]
**The [[Welsh Government]] announces a ban on [[Greyhound racing]] in [[Wales]] following cross-party calls for a ban on the sport which has been criticized for its [[animal cruelty]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c241p7pnmdzo (BBC News)]
*[[Iran–United Kingdom relations]]
**An [[Iran]]ian [[Judicial system of the Islamic Republic of Iran|court]] charges a [[United Kingdom|British]] couple who were arrested and jailed last month with [[espionage]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/iran-says-jailed-british-couple-charged-with-espionage/a-71652819 (DW)]
*[[$Libra cryptocurrency scandal]]
**A judge in [[Argentina]] orders investigations into potential [[fraud]] by [[President of Argentina|President]] [[Javier Milei]] following his brief social media promotion of a [[cryptocurrency]] that collapsed in value hours after promotion. [https://apnews.com/article/argentina-milei-cryptocurrency-fraud-charges-3f572a5f294d7c25437a08151798b917 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Second cabinet of Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States Senate]] confirms businessman [[Howard Lutnick]] as the [[United States Secretary of Commerce|Secretary of Commerce]] in a 51–45 vote. [https://apnews.com/article/howard-lutnick-trump-tariffs-commerce-department-9788590bbee10d09d3cb91822b0c9687 (AP)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[NASA]]'s [[Center for Near-Earth Object Studies]] announces that the chances of [[asteroid]] [[2024 YR4]] impacting [[Earth]] on 22 December 2032 has increased to 3.1% (1-in-32) following further observations of its orbital trajectory. It has now surpassed the threat of [[99942 Apophis]] which once had a 2.7% chance of hitting Earth during 2004 before later being ruled out. [https://www.livescience.com/space/asteroids/chance-of-city-killer-asteroid-2024-yr4-smashing-into-earth-rises-yet-again-to-3-1-percent-nasa-reports (Live Science)] [https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/15/science/asteroid-2024-yr4-earth-tracking/index.html (CNN)]
